title: Harnessing the Power of LLMs Locally: Mithun Hunsur
talk_summary: This is a 2023-era introduction to lm.rs, a Rust library for running quantized open models locally, covering tradeoffs of local vs cloud inference (cost, latency, privacy, fine-tuning) and three demo apps including a Discord bot and a fine-tuned data-extraction model. It contains no agent-orchestration, review, or eval techniques; the only transferable ideas are cheap small fine-tuned models for narrow tasks and local inference for high-volume structured extraction.

takeaways.technique: Fine-tune a small model for a narrow high-volume task instead of prompting a big cloud model
takeaways.what_they_do: For extracting dates from millions of Wikipedia pages, they generated a representative dataset with GPT-3, built a correction tool, and fine-tuned a small model so the task became a cheap, fast, consistent function call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: handling millions of dates is just too expensive and slow so I decided I'd find CH my own model

takeaways.technique: Route by task narrowness, not just by price tier
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues smaller focused models can beat large general models on specific problems, and that local/owned models make per-token cost irrelevant for high-volume work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a smaller more focused model may be able to solve problems better than a large General model

takeaways.technique: Self-contained static binaries to avoid dependency hell in sandboxes
takeaways.what_they_do: Ships inference as a single Rust binary so deployment needs no Python/torch environment, which they call out as the main pain of Python-based local inference.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you spend hours just trying to sort out your your cond your pip your pipen it's awful

takeaways.technique: Reuse a persistent session instead of re-sending context each call
takeaways.what_they_do: Notes that sessions can be kept alive across queries so conversation context need not be re-ingested, versus creating and discarding a session per request.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't need to keep ring the context
